outputText: {"tagline":"Make room for both","hook":"We keep saying “either is fine” until the plan belongs to the loudest person in the room. Jupiter widens our sense of what is possible, and in Libra that confidence grows between people through a fair counteroffer, a thoughtful compromise, or a choice that gives both sides a real say. For about a year, growth comes less through going it alone and more through making room without making ourselves smaller.","lived":"A dinner plan starts to tilt when the same person chooses the date, finds the place, and keeps adjusting so nobody else has to be uncomfortable. This time, we stop before the reservation is made: everyone names one real preference, two people compromise on timing, and someone else handles the booking. The plan takes longer to settle, but it belongs to all of us, and the evening feels easier because no one had to disappear to make it happen.","turn":"The gift becomes the problem when we ask for one more opinion after the choice is clear, then say yes because disagreement feels impolite. The conversation gets delayed, the plan gets cancelled, or one person ends up carrying a one-sided agreement. A fair agreement can survive an honest no.","moves":["Before a shared decision, let each person name one preference, one limit, and one place they can bend.","When two options are equally good, choose the one that shares effort more fairly and set a firm time to decide.","After a compromise, say the agreement aloud so hidden resentment can surface before the plan is confirmed."]}
